issues.title: GUARD1: fleet-guard caches a NEGATIVE reservation lookup for 30 s, so an edit right after reserving is refused (UPHILL from jev, 2x)
issues.description:
## Finding (UPHILL from jev, 2026-10-04, second occurrence that day; first: scripts/test_bead_lint.py)
fleet-guard refused two edits (jev ROADMAP.md, MISSION-AUDIT.md) with "tracked edits require an active exclusive Agent Mail reservation", while Agent Mail `check_file_reservation_conflicts` showed both held exclusively by the editor BrownGoose (own_active ids 122295/122296, conflict_free=true). The same edit succeeded moments later after a re-read, with no reservation change.

## Root cause (read from source, origin/main src/fleet-guard/reservations.ts)
Not the file tag: the guard caches the lookup per (project, agent, path), and NEGATIVE results too: `cache.set(key, { expiresAt: now + CACHE_TTL_MS, result })` at line 270 with `CACHE_TTL_MS = 30_000` (line 45) runs whether `result.covered` is true or false. An edit attempted before the reservation exists (or in the moment Agent Mail had not committed it) caches `covered:false` for 30 s, so every edit in that window is refused even after the reservation is granted. The "re-read" fixed it only because it took longer than 30 s. The same holds at the early lookup (lines 248-252).

## Change
Cache only positive results (covered:true; a reservation lasts until its expiry, so a short positive cache is safe), or on a negative result re-query once before blocking. A block message names the cached-at time if one is ever served from cache. This is jev's report fixed at the foundation; every profile gets it through the plugin (PROF1R).

## Landing contract
Work on main with Agent Mail reservations; `git commit --only` your paths; push after the pre-push gate. Done = on origin/main, CI green, acceptance re-run by a different pane with output cited at the exact sha. Ceremony bound: nothing here may pause product work beyond one sitting; anything that gates nothing is deleted at the weekly audit.
issues.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Positive: the sequence "edit (no reservation) -> refused; reserve; edit within 30 s" is ALLOWED on the second edit; test in tests/ using an injected clock and lookup.
- [ ] Planted negative: with a reservation held by ANOTHER agent, the edit is still refused (the positive-only cache must not open a hole); restoring negative caching makes the positive test RED.
- [ ] Independent/real machine: a non-author reproduces jev's sequence live in a real OMP profile with the plugin loaded (after PROF1R) and cites the allowed edit inside 30 s.
- [ ] No-Claim: fixing the cache does not prove Agent Mail's own reservation lookup is consistent under load.

issues.title: PROF1: kit rules and extensions in every OMP profile: one plugin store, per-profile links via apply plugin/update with receipt and undo
issues.description:
## Why
Josh asked for the long-term fix so we do not run into this on every install. The cause is structural: the kit installs its rules and extensions as a plugin, OMP keeps plugins per profile, and the kit only ever touches the default profile.

## Evidence (measured 2026-10-04 ~00:55Z, OMP 18.6.0, omp-kit 0.2.5, Josh's machine)
OMP's plugin root is per profile: `getPluginsDir()` = `dirs.rootSubdir("plugins")` under the active profile's config root (`@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/src/dirs.ts:121,673`). `omp [--profile P] ttsr list --json` + `plugin list --json` over all 17 profiles (scratch `omp-test/var/agent-tmp/pane1.99514/ttsr.<profile>.json`):
- default: 52 rules, 22 from `~/.omp/plugins/node_modules/omp-kit-companion` (0.2.5), 4 plugin extensions.
- every named profile (agy, claude, codex, codex-lean, codex-lean-undo-test, glm, grok, jev-lab, muse, nv-deepseek-flash, nv-glm, nv-glm-flash, nv-kimi, omp-test, omp-test2, p15-fake): 32 rules, 0 from the plugin, no plugin installed; 5 come from Josh's Sep 22-24 legacy copies in `~/.agents/rules`.
Fleet panes run `omp --profile codex|muse|claude` (ps of %10 %42 %43 %15 %37 %57 %53). So no live worker loads any 0.2.x kit rule or any plugin extension (fleet-guard, kit-callback, kit-save-guard, kit-guard-optin). Only default-profile panes (`omp --auto-approve`: jev %56, localbench %55) do.
This is why each release "does not take": the documented install is `omp plugin install github:JYeswak/omp-kit-companion#vX` (default profile only), and doctor's `installed_rules` compares `~/.agents/rules` bytes (DEGRADED: matching 0, missing 17, drifted 6), then recommends `apply rules --plan`, which refuses `RULE_COLLISION`.

## Change
1. One kit-owned store per release: the installed release already ships package.json, rules/, extensions/ and src/fleet-guard/ (archive carries package.json since G1). Store under the install prefix (e.g. `<prefix>/releases/<ver>/plugin`), never in scratch.
2. `omp-kit apply plugin --plan|--apply [--profile P ...]`: for each covered profile, `omp --profile P plugin link <store>` (native: dir symlink + runtime config entry, `pi-coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/manager.ts:890-944`). One receipt row per profile recording the previous state (absent, npm/git install vX, link to path) and an undo that restores it. A profile with an existing npm/git install of the same name converts only if the plan shows it. Skipped profiles are named with reasons.
3. `update --apply` relinks every covered profile to the new store; its postcheck runs PROF2's coverage check; undo relinks the previous store. L8 (rz5.80) then gets this for free.
4. README and docs/usage.md install text: say plainly that bare `omp plugin install` covers only the default profile; point to `apply plugin`.

## Acceptance (isolated HOME, real omp)
- default + 3 named profiles (one DUAL_CONFIG): plan lists 4 rows (or names the skip); apply makes `omp --profile P ttsr list --json` show the 22 kit rules with paths under the store for each covered profile, and `plugin list --json` the 4 extensions.
- Undo: each profile's plugins dir and lock file hash-identical to before (hashes cited).
- update store A to store B relinks all; planted: one profile's link target deleted makes the postcheck PARTIAL naming it, and undo still restores.
- Planted: one profile's plugins dir unwritable makes that profile REFUSED; the others apply; the receipt names it.

No-Claim: matcher and listing evidence do not prove a live block (PI1/G4).

## Landing contract
Done = merged to omp-kit-companion `main` with CI green and acceptance re-run by someone other than the implementer, output cited at the exact commit. Work on `main` with Agent Mail reservations (no branches/worktrees), `git commit --only` your paths, push after the pre-push gate. Diffs touching tests/, scripts/ladder.sh, checkers/, .github/ get reviewed separately (no weakened assertion, no new skip, no regenerated golden). Scratch under the repo's var/agent-tmp/<label>.<pid>/ with .owner.

issues.title: LOAD2: machine load census: doctor --scope load + load watch service attributing load to session/pane/agent/repo and system groups
issues.description:
## Why
Josh 2026-10-03: "system wide awareness as to whats building and whats causing the load". Today it took a manual top+lsof pass to learn that the load was macOS itself (system_installd 74%, Spotlight, Time Machine), Terminal+tmux+ntm ~107%, OMP text-predict daemons ~52%, and the agent sessions (jev 42, uds 41, omp-test 35, cfsios 22, localbench 17 % CPU), with 36 tsserver and 21 pyright LSP processes.

## Change
1. `omp-kit doctor --scope load [--json]`: read-only census: load avg vs ncpu, CPU user/sys/idle, memory pressure (memory_pressure), disk IOPS; top consumers grouped by tmux session > pane > agent > repo (map processes to panes by walking ppid to tmux pane_pid; cwd only as fallback), plus system groups (Spotlight, Time Machine, softwareupdate, WindowServer, Terminal); LSP fleet counts per session; heavy-work jobs from LOAD1's ledger (running and queued, by label/repo/agent). Verdict OK/CONTENDED with the reason.
2. `omp-kit load watch`: a kit service (S6's renderer pattern, run-at-load, interval 60 s) appending one census line per minute to census.jsonl (rotated at 10 MB) and writing census.json; flags CONTENDED for 3 consecutive minutes and names the top 3 causes.
3. Cheap: one sample must cost < 1 % of one core (ps once, tmux list-panes once; no lsof per pid; no top -l 2 loops).
## Shared contract (LOAD1 writes, LOAD2 reads)
State dir: $XDG_STATE_HOME/omp-kit/load (default ~/.local/state/omp-kit/load), mode 0700.
- jobs/<id>.json: {id, pid, process_start, label, repo, cwd, agent, tmux_pane, argv, state: queued|running, queued_at, started_at}; removed on exit; stale entries (pid dead or process_start mismatch, reuse S6's owner-liveness check) are reaped by any reader.
- Slots: N running jobs max; a slot is held by a live running job entry; admission under a lock-dir mutex (no flock on macOS).

issues.title: LOAD1: machine-wide heavy-work admission gate (omp-kit heavy -- cmd): slots, contention-aware queueing, nice 10, visible status
issues.description:
## Why
Josh 2026-10-03: the machine is near-unusable under load; heavy work (bun test suites, ladder, bun check, cargo, CLI compiles, archive gates) starts concurrently from ~30 agent panes in 6 sessions with no admission control. CPU sample: 65% idle overall but bursts and I/O stall interactive use.

## Change
`omp-kit heavy [--label L] [--no-wait] -- <cmd...>`: machine-wide admission gate for heavy work.
1. Register a queued job entry; wait until (running < slots) AND the machine is not contended (cpu idle >= min, load/core <= max); print a status line every 30 s (position, running jobs by label/repo, contention reason). Never a silent wait.
2. Run the command under nice 10 with the job entry marked running; propagate exit code; release on exit and on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
3. --no-wait or max_wait_s exceeded: exit 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL) with 'deferred: <reason>' so agents do other work.
4. Wire it: the pre-push fresh gate's cli-compile and focused-suite steps, scripts/ladder.sh, and the bun test tests/cli invocation documented in CONTRIBUTING run through it. This supersedes LC1 .60's Agent Mail slot (machine-wide, not per project, and no service dependency).
## Shared contract (LOAD1 writes, LOAD2 reads)
State dir: $XDG_STATE_HOME/omp-kit/load (default ~/.local/state/omp-kit/load), mode 0700.
- jobs/<id>.json: {id, pid, process_start, label, repo, cwd, agent, tmux_pane, argv, state: queued|running, queued_at, started_at}; removed on exit; stale entries (pid dead or process_start mismatch, reuse S6's owner-liveness check) are reaped by any reader.
- Slots: N running jobs max; a slot is held by a live running job entry; admission under a lock-dir mutex (no flock on macOS).
Config: ~/.config/omp-kit/load.json {slots (default 2 until MT4 .65 measures it), nice: 10, max_wait_s: 900, contention: {cpu_idle_min_pct: 15, load_per_core_max: 2.5}}. Machine: hw.ncpu=32.
Never use taskpolicy -b / background QoS: localbench measured 0 CPU for 40+ min under load (stalled all landings 4 h). Use nice.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Planted: with slots=1, two concurrent `heavy -- sleep 2` runs serialize (second starts after first exits); a killed holder (SIGKILL) frees its slot for the next reader (stale reap); a planted contention reading queues even with a free slot; --no-wait under contention exits 75.
- [ ] The pre-push gate and ladder go through it (shown by a job entry during a real push).
- [ ] No full suites run to verify this while the machine is loaded: targeted tests only.

issues.title: RX2: literal-first rule shape and escaped-boundary anchors: make every bash rule linear and live-correct
issues.description:
## Why
RX1 measurements (see RX1): 5 kit rules are quadratic per check and the realistic heredoc stream costs 14.2 s of synchronous regex CPU in OMP. Root shape (regex-engineering §2 shape 2, §3 pass 1): conditions BEGIN with a long variable-length lookbehind (the echo/printf/quote exclusion), so JSC runs that lookbehind at every input position and scans back toward the start: O(n) per position, O(n^2) per check. Separately PI4/PI3 proved \b-anchored words miss live, because OMP matches JSON-encoded arguments where a newline/tab becomes backslash-n/backslash-t (\bgit fails after \n; e1fe957 fixed only kit-test-skip).

## Change (one pass per rule, same files, one owner)
1. Literal-first: rewrite `(?<!CTX)LIT REST` as `LIT REST` with the context check moved AFTER the literal: `LIT(?<!CTX LIT)REST` (JS lookbehind is unbounded, so this is verdict-equivalent) or bound the lookbehind. The engine then fails fast at every position lacking the literal's first char.
2. Escaped boundaries: every leading `\b` before a command word also accepts a preceding escaped `\n`/`\t` in the JSON form, e.g. `(?:\b|(?<=\\[nt]))`.
3. Add fire rows for multi-line and tab-indented variants of each bash rule; regenerate MANIFEST in the same commit.

## Acceptance
- [ ] RX1 gate PASS on all rules (ratio <= 2.6 or under the noise floor; stream total <= 500 ms), table cited before/after with load.
- [ ] G2/G3 331+/331+ PASS; metamorphic zero-break; L9 oracle (scripts/differential-oracle.ts) 0 unexpected mismatches.
- [ ] Live G4 scenario: a bash call whose second line is `git push --force` is interrupted on OMP latest (and was NOT before, cited).
- [ ] No-claim: equivalence is proven on the corpus + oracle + generated inputs, not for all strings.

issues.title: RX1: regex budget gate: every rule timed in Bun on near-miss shapes and a realistic live stream, plus a literal-first lint
issues.description:
## Why (reality check round 6, 2026-10-03, measured)
OMP runs rule conditions as plain JS RegExp in Bun (JavaScriptCore), with no timeout (capability/rule.ts:363 compileRuleCondition). In live sessions OMP 18.5.0 appends every streamed delta to a per-tool buffer and re-runs every rule on the WHOLE buffer (export/ttsr.ts:439-449 checkDelta), synchronously. Regex-engineering skill (~/.agents/skills/regex-engineering) §2/§4/§7: test in the engine that ships; double the near-miss length (x2 linear, x4 quadratic); speed claims are measurements.
Coordinator probe on origin/main 9a91486 rules, Bun 1.4.0, OMP 18.5.0 compileRuleCondition, load ~12 (rc3/rx-measure.ts, rc3/rx-stream.ts):
- Quadratic per single check (ms at 4k/8k/16k): kit-relative-path-not-cwd 216/792/3132 (semicolon run, raw); kit-no-force-push 118/588/2112 (backslash run, JSON = live encoding); kit-gate-must-name-the-plant 113/512/1916 (semicolons, JSON); kit-scratch-tmp 8/32/127 (dquote run, JSON); zz-canary-scope-probe 3/15/67.
- Realistic live stream: the model writes scripts/e2e-live.sh (18.6 KB JSON) through a bash heredoc: 16-byte deltas -> 14.2 s total regex CPU in OMP's stream path (64-byte deltas -> 3.4 s); kit-close-needs-evidence alone 6.7 s (14 ms per full check).
No gate measures any of this; qzb fixed only the harness observe path.

## Change
`scripts/regex-budget.ts` (+ ladder stage + L6 pre-push when rules/ changes):
1. Near-miss scaling: every condition of every rule, compiled with OMP's compileRuleCondition, timed in Bun on shapes {single-quote run, escaped-dquote run, backslash run, space run, semicolon run, newline run, the rule's own required literal repeated without its terminator} x encodings {raw, JSON.stringify({command})} at 4k/8k/16k. FAIL when the 8k->16k ratio > 2.6 AND the 16k time > 5 ms (noise floor), naming rule/shape/encoding.
2. Stream budget: the e2e-live.sh heredoc at 16-byte deltas, all kit rules: total <= 500 ms on CI (report load average).
3. Structural lint (skill §3 pass 1): no condition may begin with a lookaround or an unbounded wildcard; every lookbehind must sit after a required literal or be bounded.
Report JSON + human table; reuse the qzb Bun harness.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Gate output on current main lists the 5 quadratic rules above and the stream total (FAIL), with load average.
- [ ] Planted: adding `condition: '(a+)+b'` to a fixture rule fails near-miss scaling naming it; a fixture rule starting with `(?<!x)` fails the lint.
- [ ] Runs in < 60 s on CI; wired into ladder.sh and the L6 changed-area map for rules/*.
- [ ] No-claim: a passing gate proves bounded cost on these shapes in Bun/JSC, not on every possible input.

issues.title: ID1: agent identity primitive for every repo: pane identity at spawn, br actor injected and enforced, Agent trailer on commits, grader != implementer guard
issues.description:
## Ask (Josh 2026-10-04 ~20:5xZ, via uds %57 uphill)
An AGENT IDENTITY primitive in the kit, for all repos.

## Defect (uds evidence)
For days every uds worker wrote br as 'SapphireIsland' (pane 1's name), because uds AGENTS.md said "every br write passes --actor SapphireIsland". Self-closes and self-grades were therefore invisible: 81kq.6 self-closed at 20:37. Fixed locally in uds 2925d93.
Same class here: in the omp-kit tracker, comments without --actor show author 'josh' (the OS user). Round A R2b misread DustyRidge's L8 pause note (#574) as Josh's own work because of it.

## Facts (uds probe)
br attributes ONLY via --actor. BR_AGENT_NAME exists in the binary but does not set the comment author (BR_AGENT_NAME=IdentityProbe with no --actor gave author=josh). BR_HARNESS and BR_MODEL exist.

## Shape (uds proposal)
1. At pane spawn, the kit resolves the pane's Agent Mail name and exports AGENT_NAME, plus the br and uds actor variables.
2. A br wrapper or shim injects --actor $AGENT_NAME, and refuses a write whose actor differs from the caller's identity.
3. Git commits carry an 'Agent: <name>' trailer, added by a prepare-commit-msg hook.
4. Close and grade guard: the grader's actor must differ from the implementer's (taken from the claim and commit trailers); otherwise refuse.
5. A doctor check flags one actor writing from more than one pane in the same hour.
6. Upstream ask for beads_rust: honor an env default actor (BR_ACTOR) on every write, and record pane and harness.

## Why it matters
MP3's reviewer rule and ADOPT1's "the implementer can't approve their own close" rule both assume br knows who wrote what. Today it does not. uds's local fix stays until the kit lands, then uds deletes its copy.
## Landing contract
Work on main with Agent Mail reservations; `git commit --only` your paths; push after the pre-push gate. Done = on origin/main, CI green, acceptance re-run by a different pane with output cited at the exact sha. Ceremony bound: nothing here may pause product work beyond one sitting; anything that gates nothing is deleted at the weekly audit.

- [ ] Commit trailer: a commit made in a kit repo carries 'Agent: <name>'; a planted commit with a mismatched trailer fails the hook.

- [ ] Doctor flags one actor writing from more than one pane within an hour (planted shared-name case, RED) and is quiet for distinct names.

## Ask (Josh, 2026-10-04)
"how - along the way - are we proving without a doubt - that what we build gets applied and is proven to work across our own fleet in dogfooded efforts? is that a part of our bead lint proving ground on this projects along the way?"

## Gap (measured 2026-10-04)
- The strict policy (.beads/policy.yaml) enforces: every box ticked, a transition comment, a min_reviewers gate report. All three are recorded CLAIMS. Nothing checks that a "Live/wired" box points at evidence that exists, or that the change is still loaded on the fleet.
- `br gate report --status pass --provider reviewer:<x>` accepts any provider string. The coordinator closed 4 beads today with provider reviewer:josh-grill-q3, which is legitimate here but shows the gate cannot tell a review from a label.
- Proof the gap is real: 138 beads closed while the kit plugin was enabled in 1 of 17 profiles, so 16 profiles loaded zero kit rules and zero extensions. Closures passed; fleet adoption was zero.
- Planned beads report pieces (PROF2 rz5.82 profile loads, MP2 rz5.94 mission audit, MP5 rz5.97 daily scoreboard) but none ties a closed bead to a re-runnable fleet probe.

## Shape
1. Every bead that ships behavior names an adoption probe in its acceptance: a command whose output proves the change is live on the fleet (rule fires in profile P, service S loaded, gate refuses a plant in repo R).
2. Close lint: moving to closed is refused when the bead has no probe, or when the probe output cited in the transition comment does not match a fresh run (re-run by the gate, not pasted).
3. Fleet replay: a recurring job (MP5 cadence) re-runs every closed bead's probe across all profiles and repos. A failing probe reopens the bead with the output (demotions are always allowed).
4. Retro audit: the 138 closed beads are classified PROVEN-LIVE / NOT-WIRED / NO-PROBE; NOT-WIRED reopen.
## Landing contract
Work on main with Agent Mail reservations; `git commit --only` your paths; push after the pre-push gate. Done = on origin/main, CI green, acceptance re-run by a different pane with output cited at the exact sha. Ceremony bound: nothing here may pause product work beyond one sitting; anything that gates nothing is deleted at the weekly audit.
issues.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Probe field: a bead's acceptance can name an adoption probe (command + expected output), and `br show` / doctor list it.
- [ ] Close lint refuses a close with no probe on a behavior bead (planted, RED) and accepts docs/process beads marked probe:n/a with a reason.
- [ ] Close lint re-runs the probe and refuses when the fresh output does not match (planted: a probe for a rule disabled in the profile, RED).
- [ ] Gate provider check: a min_reviewers pass from the implementer's own pane is refused; a reviewer-fresh-context:<model> pass is labelled (ties to MP3 rz5.95).
- [ ] Fleet replay job re-runs every closed bead's probe across every configured profile (enumerated at run time; 17 on 2026-10-04) and the five repos; a planted regression reopens the bead with the output attached.
- [ ] Retro audit of all closed beads: counts of PROVEN-LIVE / NOT-WIRED / NO-PROBE cited; every NOT-WIRED bead reopened with its evidence.
- [ ] Live/wired: the replay job is loaded and ran on Josh's machine at least 3 consecutive days; its rows feed the MP5 scoreboard.
- [ ] Independent/real machine: a non-implementer plants one unwired closed bead and shows the replay reopens it.
- [ ] No-Claim: a passing probe proves the change is loaded and fires on its probe case, not that it helps; benefit is the learning loop's job.
- [ ] Cost and load bound (Josh 2026-10-04: fast, safe, cost-balanced): the replay runs locally (no GitHub Actions), through `omp-kit heavy` at nice 10, staggered, with a per-probe time cap and a total budget (default 10 min/day); it skips a run when load is above 2.5x cores and records SKIPPED-LOAD. Only probes whose bead's code or the profile changed since the last green run are re-run daily; the full replay runs weekly.

issues.title: PUB1: public-by-default kit rule for every repo: no secrets, no home paths, config not literals, neutral fixtures, publishability gate on push
issues.description:
## Ask (Josh, 2026-10-04 ~20:1xZ, via uds %57 uphill), verbatim
"build with a public repo in mind; we shouldn't create work that is personalized as much as we can help it; if we build with public in mind on everything we touch, going public is easy."
Plans and beads may be public; Josh's name is public; ONLY secrets are off-limits.

## Rule (all repos, shipped by the kit)
(a) No secrets in any tracked file, bead or comment; a secret scan runs at pre-commit and pre-push.
(b) No absolute home paths in tracked code or docs: use $HOME, ~, or config.
(c) Machine-, worker- and person-specific values come from config or env with neutral defaults, never literals.
(d) Tests use neutral fixtures (worker-1, example.invalid, 192.0.2.x), not real hostnames or IPs.
(e) Doctor and push gate: the repo's publishability check (secrets, home paths, IPs, hostnames) runs on every push, so any repo can flip public with no scrub sprint.

## Why
uds evidence: today's scrub sprint (PublicUds + NameScrub, ~2 h) is the cost of not doing this. The kit itself is public (omp-kit-companion).

## Shape
A kit TTSR rule that fires when an agent writes a literal home path, private IP or secret-shaped token into a tracked file, plus a `publishability` check in doctor and the pre-push fresh-gate. The check is local: it does not depend on GitHub Actions, so it costs nothing on private repos (CI1 rz5.104).
## Non-goals
Rewriting history of already-public repos; renaming people; blocking paths in untracked scratch (var/agent-tmp).
## Landing contract
Work on main with Agent Mail reservations; `git commit --only` your paths; push after the pre-push gate. Done = on origin/main, CI green, acceptance re-run by a different pane with output cited at the exact sha. Ceremony bound: nothing here may pause product work beyond one sitting; anything that gates nothing is deleted at the weekly audit.
issues.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Rule file in rules/ with fire rows from real occurrences (the uds scrub sprint diff and this tracker) and quiet rows (\$HOME, ~, config lookups, neutral fixtures); passes RX1 budget and G2/G3/metamorphic.
- [ ] Secret scan at pre-commit and pre-push refuses a planted secret-shaped token in a tracked file (RED), and passes after removal.
- [ ] Planted absolute home path in tracked code makes the publishability check RED; the same path in var/agent-tmp is ignored.
- [ ] Planted private IP or real hostname in a test fixture makes the check RED; worker-1 / 192.0.2.x pass.
- [ ] Doctor reports publishability per repo (findings with file:line), and the pre-push gate runs it on every push.
- [ ] Live/wired: the rule fires in a real session in a non-kit repo (uds or jev) through the installed kit plugin, and the push gate refuses a planted home path on a real push attempt; transcript cited.
- [ ] Independent/real machine: a non-implementer runs the check on omp-kit-companion, uds, jev and localbench and cites the counts; any finding is filed in that repo.
- [ ] No-Claim: the check reduces leaks of known shapes; it does not prove a repo holds no secrets.
- [ ] Retire local copies: uds runs the kit check in place of scripts/publishability-gate.sh, and deletes that script, with its 8 selftest legs passing against the kit check first.

issues.title: DISPATCH1: bv --robot-next picks a disconnected P2 bead (si4) while the certified PageRank top is RX1; dispatch must not trust robot-next until explained
issues.description:
## Finding (2026-10-04 ~18:30Z, coordinator, pagerank-bead-triage certificate)
Certificate over the open omp-kit DAG (63+ open beads, blocking edges, A->B = A depends on B, damping 0.85): residual_l1 4.69e-10 < 1e-9, node-order invariant, predicted top = ompkit-kxdy (RX1). Probe: `/Users/josh/Developer/flywheel/.flywheel/scripts/bv-readiness-probe.sh pagerank-cert --pagerank-graph-fixture /Users/josh/Developer/omp-test/var/agent-tmp/pane1.99514/pagerank-fixture.json --json` -> failure_class bv_top_mismatch.
`bv --robot-next` (v0.25.2) returns ompkit-systemd-interval-trigger-state-si4 (P2, no edges at all, score 0.0917, only reason "Currently unclaimed"). bv's OWN graph pagerank ranks it low (0.00236 vs RX1 0.01663, MP3 0.00658). Hypothesis "bv ranks unclaimed only" was tested and is FALSE: among unclaimed ready beads the certified top is MP3 rz5.95, not si4. Cause not established.
## Consequence
Until resolved, dispatch follows the certified ranking, not `bv --robot-next`; claim_top from bv is not br-claim-admissible.
## Change
Find what drives robot-next's score (recency of update? si4 was updated in the owner normalization minutes earlier), then either use `br scheduler`/the certificate in the coordinator path or file a stranger repro upstream on bv (Dicklesworthstone), via the zeststream-pr issue path.
issues.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Cause named: what drives `bv --robot-next`'s pick is named (the field it actually ranks on).
- [ ] Reproduction: a fixture (e.g. two-bead) where robot-next disagrees with bv's own pagerank reproduces the cause.
- [ ] Certified ranking on live tracker: the pagerank certificate is rerun on the live omp-kit tracker (residual and certified top cited) and compared to robot-next's id.
- [ ] Resolution: either the coordinator path uses `br scheduler`/the certificate, or a stranger repro is filed upstream on bv via the zeststream-pr issue path (link cited).
- [ ] Planted negative (probe): a fixture whose bv_top_id disagrees with the certified top fails with bv_top_mismatch (keep it red).
- [ ] Planted negative (fail-closed dispatch): on the live tracker, a planted/observed mismatch between `bv --robot-next` and the certified top results in NO claim made from robot-next's claim_top until the certified ranking agrees or the dispatch path is corrected; RED if dispatch claims bv's pick.
- [ ] Independent/real machine: a non-author reruns the certificate and robot-next on the live tracker on Josh's machine through the real dispatch path, and cites both ids and the dispatch decision.
- [ ] No-Claim: centrality ranks prerequisite leverage; it does not decide value. Priority and the mission's pillars still govern. The MP2 doctor MATCH/MISMATCH integration is accepted in rz5.94, not here.
- [ ] Admissible comparison: the certificate check compares bv --robot-next against the certified top of the claim-admissible set (open, ready, unassigned), and a planted claimed top does not trigger a mismatch while a planted admissible mismatch does (RED).

issues.title: GATE1: pre-push gate runs the working tree's fresh-gate.sh, so one agent's uncommitted gate edit refuses every other agent's push
issues.description:
## Evidence (2026-10-04 01:31Z, shared checkout ~/Developer/omp-kit-companion)
`git push origin HEAD:main` of 9f48b57 (AGENTS.md only) was refused: `RED cli-compile producer_rc=2`, `UNKNOWN_FLAG: Unknown flag: --label`, `40-omp-kit-fresh-gate exited with status 1`.
Cause: `.git/hooks/hooks.d/pre-push/40-omp-kit-fresh-gate` does `exec "$ROOT/scripts/fresh-gate.sh" --commit "$local_sha"`, i.e. it runs the WORKING TREE copy of the gate. At that moment `scripts/fresh-gate.sh` and `scripts/ladder.sh` carried GoldCompass's uncommitted LOAD1 edit (steps wrapped in `src/cli.ts heavy --label ...`), while the archive of the pushed commit has no `heavy` command (`git show HEAD:scripts/fresh-gate.sh | grep -c 'heavy --label'` = 0). One agent's dirty gate edit blocks every other agent's push from the shared checkout.

## Change
The pre-push gate runs gate code from a committed tree, never the working tree. Use the base the push lands on (`origin/main`, already accepted) so a commit cannot weaken the gate that judges it, and a peer's dirty files cannot affect it. A commit that changes the gate itself is judged by the old gate; CI on main then runs the new one.

## Acceptance
- Planted: a dirty, uncommitted edit to scripts/fresh-gate.sh that would fail (e.g. `exit 1` at the top) does not affect a push of an unrelated commit (gate GREEN); removing the fix makes it RED.
- Planted: a commit that deletes a gate step is still judged by the base's gate (the step still runs).
- The installed hook (kit hook installer and docs) is updated so every checkout gets it.

- [ ] Planted negative (A, worktree isolation): append `exit 1` to a DIRTY, uncommitted scripts/fresh-gate.sh; the push of an unrelated commit must still PASS. Reverting the archive fix must make this test RED. (This is the bug GATE1 exists for; it was observed 2026-10-04 01:31Z when GoldCompass's uncommitted heavy edit refused an AGENTS.md push.)
- [ ] Planted negative (B, no self-weakening): a pushed commit that deletes or no-ops a gate step must still be judged by the BASE gate (origin/main's committed fresh-gate.sh), so the deleted step still runs. 68745210cc runs the gate from the pushed commit's own archive and is expected to FAIL this case; fix by running gate code from the base archive (or both base and head, base authoritative).
- [ ] Independent/real machine: a non-implementer runs (A) and (B) on a scratch clone with a bare origin and cites hook exit codes; the hook installer puts the same chain into every checkout.
- [ ] No-Claim: a green hook proves only the committed gate's checks for that sha; it does not prove the working tree is clean or that CI on main is green.

issues.title: LAND1: shared-checkout landing primitive: commit exactly my reserved paths onto fresh origin/main, repo-declared check, push on pass (design over save-ops + uds push-own-hunks)
issues.description:
## Ask (Josh, 2026-10-04)
- "i would rather not work in short lived feature branches if we can help it - that is what agentmail file reservations are for"
- On %57's proposal to port uds `scripts/push-own-hunks.sh` into omp-kit: "perhaps we need to design and validate this using skills like /skill:git-repo-janitor and our save ops processes that were turned off because they aren't finished properly?" then "draft it up into our beads dag properly - dont take it on yourself".

## Problem
Agents share one checkout on `main` and must commit only their reserved paths. Doing that by hand with the shared index goes wrong: CreamFern's hand-built candidate in uds pulled in foreign `main.rs` hunks and a `claims.toml` deletion. The fleet needs one landing primitive that (1) commits exactly the caller's reserved paths onto fresh origin/main without touching the shared index or HEAD, (2) runs the repo's own check against that exact commit, (3) pushes only on pass, never forced, and (4) emits a typed verdict.

## Inputs to design from (read, do not assume)
- uds `scripts/push-own-hunks.sh` (8b37b66, 194 lines, by the control-plane orchestrator %57): scratch `GIT_INDEX_FILE` read-tree of fresh `<remote>/main`, `git add -A -- <paths>` from the worktree, commit-msg hook, `commit-tree`, rch `cargo check` on touched crates at the exact sha, `git push <sha>:refs/heads/main` (never forced) only on pass, final `PUSH verdict=PUSHED|REFUSED|UNRUN reason=... sha=... base=... check=PASS|FAIL|UNRUN|SKIP` line, exit 0/1/77.
- save-ops (`zs save` -> `~/.zeststream/commons/substrate/scripts/zs`): verbs save, snapshot, scope-clean, auto-push-preflight, park/on (throwaway-index snapshot), apply with evidence pack and idempotency key. Health: `zs save doctor --json` did not return within 60 s (2026-10-04 00:57Z). The raw-git save-ops PreToolUse gate was UNREGISTERED in the 2026-06-10 hook inventory; flywheel-uqwbc (save-ops class) open since 2026-05-27. Josh: switched off because it is not finished. Find out which verbs work, which do not, and why, with commands run.
- git-repo-janitor / git-stash-janitor discipline: reversible-before-mutation, typed refusal, never stash/pop/reset in a shared tree, verbatim authorization for destructive steps.
- Already in omp-kit: fleet-guard `git.ts` (main-only, blocks blanket staging), `reservations.ts` (Agent Mail lookup; fails open when the identity is unknown), kit-save-guard (session-end warning), the L6 pre-push gate.

## Design questions (answer in this bead with evidence before code)
1. Home: omp-kit command (public; cannot depend on private HOME substrate) vs save-ops verb vs per-repo script. Who calls it: agents directly, fleet-guard nudges, uds wrapper.
2. Ownership: the named paths must be covered by the caller's active exclusive Agent Mail reservations; otherwise REFUSED. What happens with an unknown identity (today fleet-guard fails open)?
3. Check: repo-declared command (e.g. `.omp/push-check`), trusted by hash the way watch specs are; a changed file is inactive until re-registered; no registered check pushes with `check=SKIP` stated in the verdict.
4. After the push the shared checkout's local `main` is behind origin/main while its worktree already holds the pushed content. Show, by running it, how HEAD catches up without stash/reset and without disturbing other agents' dirty paths.
5. What save-ops pieces to reuse, fix, or retire, and how the private substrate and the public kit avoid two implementations of one concept.

## Acceptance (temp repo with a bare origin; each planted negative must go RED with its guard removed)
- (a) happy path: PUSHED; shared index and HEAD byte-identical before/after; other dirty paths untouched; origin/main = base + exactly the named paths.
- (b) path not reserved by the caller: REFUSED reason=not_reserved, origin unchanged.
- (c) commit-msg hook rejects: REFUSED, nothing pushed.
- (d) check fails: REFUSED, origin unchanged.
- (e) origin advances between fetch and push: REFUSED push_rejected, never forced.
- (f) check file changed since registration: check inactive, stated in the verdict.
- (g) the CreamFern case: a foreign hunk in an unnamed path stays out of the commit.
- Then uds keeps a thin wrapper that passes its rch check, and omp-kit-companion lands through it.

Out of scope: uds `--route` (AC map + unfiltered tests vs parent) stays uds-side.

In temp repo with bare origin, implement public `omp-kit land` transaction with both reserved-path mode and `--patch <file> -m <msg>` scratch-index mode. Path mode requires every whole named path reserved; patch mode applies all-or-nothing onto fresh origin/main scratch index and includes only patch paths. TTSR rules ship in the kit plugin to every profile and fire at the moment an agent writes the risky thing, which is where AGENTS.md text fails (agents read it once, at session start, and today's sessions predate most of it). Confirmed repeated gaps from 2026-10-03 alone:
1. Landing branch work by copying files over main (MT2 fd320f4 deleted ~1,100 lines): `git checkout <ref> -- <paths>` / `cp` from a clone into the checkout -> teach git merge / git merge-file.
2. `git commit --only` with new files fails (ScarletWaterfall RX1) -> teach `git add -- <exact new paths>` first; never `add -A`/`commit -a` (dcg blocks those, but does not teach the right sequence).
3. Deleting or moving `.git/index.lock` -> teach: check the holder (`lsof`), wait if a git process holds it; only an orphan with no holder may be moved, by the coordinator.
4. Temp files in /var/folders or /tmp: mktemp/tempfile/test runners with TMPDIR unset (159 GB) -> teach: export TMPDIR to <repo>/var/agent-tmp/<label>.<pid> first (extends kit-scratch-tmp beyond redirects).
5. Workers announcing they will wait ("awaiting handoff", "waiting for <agent>", "blocked until ... releases") -> teach: take the next queue item now; report BLOCKED with NEXT.
6. Long or wide Agent Mail reservations (exclusive, ttl > 1 h, whole files not being edited) -> teach: exact paths, ttl <= 3600.
7. Reading your own reservation as someone else's (VerifyLuna/DustyRidge on src/cli.ts) -> teach: check `own_active` in check_file_reservation_conflicts.

For each gap: (a) confirm it repeats and is fleet-wide with the session corpus (`omp-kit corpus` / cass) - count occurrences across sessions and repos; (b) write a kit rule (prose reminder or tripwire, whichever the harm warrants) with fire rows from the real occurrences and quiet near-miss rows; (c) the rule passes RX1 (literal-first, linear, stream budget) and G2/G3/metamorphic/L9; (d) a live G4 scenario where possible; (e) ship in the plugin; (f) MT2 calibration watches its false-fire rate in the corpus after release.

## Ask (Josh, 2026-10-04)
"as part of omp, don't we need to be tracking prompts as part of our repeatable process? omp-kit prompt with a full library broken down - look at ntm palette, look at jfp, we can scour x and git and set up a library of prompts that each session can used, tied to various parts of the process. we can grade and upgrade the prompts against our skills library etc. we could probably use the jev repo / clef model in a variety of ways in this. work with localbench and jev repos to think about this - i keep finding prompts that I use and applying them manually, but as part of our kit, if we can give each session a library of prompts to use with instructions for providing uphill feedback if they find any gaps or issues, it will truly help to align the operating procedures in every repo."

## What exists today (measured 2026-10-04)
- OMP-native prompt files: 89 in ~/.omp/agent/prompts, copied by hand into profile prompt dirs (7 profiles hold identical copies; 9 profiles have none). Copies drift: there is no single source.
- jfp (Jeffrey Emanuel's prompt library CLI, ~/.local/bin/jfp 1.0.3): `jfp list` returns a JSON catalog (id, category, tags, author, version, content). Local notes: omp-test/jfp-catalog.md, jfp-prompts-index.md.
- ntm palette: ~/.config/ntm/command_palette.md (sections Fleet Diagnosis, Dispatch, Analysis & Review, Coding & Development, Git & Operations, Agent Coordination) plus per-session palettes (command_palette.zeststream.md, config.*.toml). ntm is OPTIONAL for omp-kit users (Josh 2026-10-04), so the palette is a source, not the delivery path.
- Delivery path that needs no new mechanism: OMP discovers `prompts/` (and `commands/`, `skills/`) inside an enabled plugin package (OMP src/discovery/omp-plugins.ts; see G1 rz5.20). The kit plugin can ship the library, and PROF1 rz5.83 puts the plugin in every profile; that replaces the hand copies.
- jev Clef model (open-weight, local, on localbench's gateway :8010): a calibrated classifier jev already uses to grade (jev README; ROADMAP pillar Local-first). Candidate grader for prompt quality and for matching a prompt to a process stage, but only where a receipt shows it matches or beats the alternative.

## Shape (to be designed WITH jev and localbench, not by omp-kit alone)
1. Library: one source in the kit (prompts/ in the plugin), each prompt with front matter: stage of the Mission Protocol arc (plan, dispatch, build, review, grade, close, learn), skills it pairs with, source/provenance (jfp id, palette section, X/GitHub URL, Josh), version.
2. Intake: sources = jfp catalog, ntm palettes, ~/.omp/agent/prompts, prompts Josh applies by hand, plus a sweep of X/GitHub; dedupe; Josh approves additions.
3. Grade and upgrade: each prompt scored against outcomes (the learning-loop horizon in ROADMAP), skills it invokes (skill library), and a classifier pass (Clef via localbench, if its receipt holds); upgrades go through the normal review.
4. Uphill: every prompt carries the instruction "if this prompt has a gap or misfires, report UPHILL <prompt id> <evidence> to omp-test %54" (MP0 rz5.92).
## Not decided here
Whether grading is omp-kit, jev or a later learning-loop project; how much of jfp to vendor (licence and attribution); per-repo prompt overrides.

## Landing contract
Work on main with Agent Mail reservations; `git commit --only` your paths; push after the pre-push gate. Done = on origin/main, CI green, acceptance re-run by a different pane with output cited at the exact sha. Ceremony bound: nothing here may pause product work beyond one sitting; anything that gates nothing is deleted at the weekly audit.

issues.description:
## Scope (first slice of ompkit-1hqq)
1. `omp-kit watchd`: per-user supervisor, Bun/TS. It hosts watchers as tasks with AbortController-scoped cancellation.
   - Process-group spawn and reap.
   - Bounded queue, log byte cap, RSS cap.
   - nice 10.
   - Heartbeat.
   - Typed start/stop rows (EC-PASS/RED/UNRUN/INFRA/TIMEOUT).
2. Spec format `.omp/watch/<name>.toml`:
   - Fields: on.fs/on.proc/on.timer, run, debounce, budget, consumer, gate, defect, retire_when, ttl.
   - Validation refuses: timer < 60 s; any missing consumer/gate/defect/retire_when.
3. `omp-kit watch add|list|status|stop`:
   - add copies the spec plus its sha256 into the user registry; a repo never activates a spec.
   - A changed repo spec shows as `stale` until re-added.
   - Single instance per (repo, spec) via lock + pid + process start time; a second add/start is a no-op that names the holder.
4. flywheel-watchers registers ONLY the supervisor launchd job (`omp-kit watchd`).
5. First real watcher: index-lock attribution.
   - Event: FSEvents/kqueue create of .git/index.lock (no ps/lsof polling).
   - On event: one debounced process snapshot.
   - retire_when = first event naming a creator; ttl 7 d.

2. Planted timeout: a run exceeding its bound -> EC-TIMEOUT row, child reaped.
3. Planted duplicate: a second `watch add` of the same spec -> no second instance; the output names the holder pid.
4. Planted fast timer (30 s) -> refused at add with a typed reason.
5. Planted repo-spec change after add -> `watch status` shows stale and the old spec keeps running unchanged.
6. Budget: an RSS-cap breach -> the watcher is stopped with a typed row; log rotation holds the byte cap.
7. Live: the index-lock watcher runs under watchd for 1 h with measured CPU < 0.5% and no ps/lsof invocations except on events (dtrace/fs_usage or exec census).

issues.description:
## Problem (census, 2026-10-03, /Users/josh/Developer/uds/var/agent-tmp/pane1-dispatch.9289/watcher-design.md)
Watchers across the fleet are ad hoc poll loops. Measured instances:
- fleet-watch.sh x3: sh loop + sleep.
- index-lock-watch.sh: ps+lsof+find every 5 s for 1 d 19 h, 765 events, named 0 creators.
- index-lock-watch.py x2: same jev repo, duplicated.
- cfsios lsof loop: every 0.3 s, unknown restarter.
- 12 orphan-style sleep processes.
- A fleet watcher that died silently.
Polling ps/lsof loads sysmond (~13k syscalls/s measured by localbench). There is no single-instance guarantee, no budget, no liveness and no retirement.

## Decision (omp-test %54, 2026-10-03)
- Runtime: Bun/TS inside omp-kit. One compiled binary on 4 targets. Cancel-correctness is proven by planted kill/timeout tests, not by language choice. Revisit Rust only on measured leaks/growth.
- Specs: may live in-repo at .omp/watch/*.toml for versioning, but a repo NEVER activates them (#13330 trust gap). 'omp-kit watch add <spec>' copies the spec into the user registry with its content hash; a changed repo spec stays inactive until re-added. The kit pack ships the standard watchers: fleet idle via tmux -C, load census, scratch reaper, browser reaper.
- Boundary: flywheel-watchers registers ONLY the supervisor launchd job ('omp-kit watchd'). omp-kit owns specs, registry, status, doctor and stop rows.
- Invariants:
  - Event-driven first (FSEvents/kqueue, process exit, tmux -C); a timer floor of 60 s, enforced by the runtime.
  - Single instance per (repo, spec): lock plus pid plus process start time.
  - Registration requires consumer/gate/defect/retire_when.
  - Every watcher runs at nice 10.
  - Queue, log bytes and RSS are bounded.
  - Typed stop rows (EC-PASS/RED/UNRUN/INFRA/TIMEOUT); process-group reap with no surviving children or orphan sleeps.
  - The supervisor reports dead watchers.
- Tripwires no-poll-under-60s and no-raw-sleep-loop are routed to LR1 ompkit-gbkj by %54.
- Sequencing: after LOAD1 ompkit-t8do and LOAD2 ompkit-w559; W2, S6 and LOAD2 fold in as watchers.

issues.title: Systemd interval lifecycle checks query path instead of timer
issues.description:

- [ ] Real systemd: On a real Linux host (e.g. aperture), `service install scratch-reaper` under user systemd leaves `omp-kit-scratch-reaper.timer` loaded and active; `service status` reports loaded and `service doctor` reports healthy; cite `systemctl --user status` output.

issues.description:
WHAT: Optimize scripts/ttsr-harness.ts --observe so a valid approximately 41 KB bash tool payload completes in under one second; leave installed OMP source untouched.

issues.title: JS1: keep the Dicklesworthstone stack current: 14 of 17 installed tools are behind and nothing updates them
issues.description:
Measured 2026-10-02 (rc3/jeff-bins.sh, rc3/jeff-bins.txt): every Dicklesworthstone tool on Josh's machine is behind its latest release, and nothing updates them. UCA covers only the agent harnesses (claude, codex, agy, grok, omp, muse).

Installed vs latest:
- ntm 1.35.1-dev vs 1.36.1
- br 0.6.0 vs 0.7.4
- bv 0.20.0 vs 0.25.2
- dcg 0.14.4 vs 0.15.2
- ubs 5.3.13 vs 5.4.17
- rch 2.0.0 vs 2.1.15
- dsr 0.1.2 vs 0.2.1
- ru 1.3.1 vs 1.5.0
- cass 0.9.0 vs 0.10.0
- cm 0.2.14 vs 0.4.0
- sbh 0.6.18 vs 0.6.24
- pt 2.1.0 vs 2.2.1
- rano 0.1.0 vs 0.2.0
- caam: a dev build vs 0.1.22

Current: am, ms, ee. Not installed: acfs, apr, xf, csctf, skillranker; frankengit has no release (pre-release).

Install sources are mixed (~/.cargo/bin, ~/.local/bin curl installers, /opt/homebrew). Jeff publishes Homebrew formulas for most of them (tap dicklesworthstone/tap: br bv caam cass cm dcg ee mcp-agent-mail ntm rch ru slb ubs xf ...), and the tap is already tapped here.

Do:
1. Choose ONE install source per tool (prefer the tap formula; keep the tool's own self-update where it has one).
2. Add the stack to a cadence updater: UCA if it can take extra targets, otherwise a kit service job (S1) running each tool's updater with a smoke test (tool --version plus its doctor), receipts, and rollback.
3. After each update, re-run the OMP integration matrix (PI1) for the tools with OMP bridges (dcg, rch, slb, am).

Do not switch install sources on the real machine without Josh's approval.

Acceptance: a currency report (installed vs latest) as a kit doctor scope; one approved update round on the real machine with receipts; the PI1 matrix still green afterwards.
issues.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Currency report: `omp-kit doctor --scope <currency scope>` is READ-ONLY and reports installed vs latest known for the stack (ntm/br/bv/dcg/ubs/rch/dsr/ru/cass/cm/sbh/pt/rano/caam, plus am/ms/ee) and points at uds for upgrades.
- [ ] Hold warning: Tools below omp-kit's holds in uds registries/upgrade_policy.toml (e.g. br >= 0.7.4) are flagged as below-hold warnings.
- [ ] Status distinctions: Unknown (no latest/version unparsable), not-installed (acfs, apr, xf, csctf, skillranker) and no-release (frankengit) are reported as such, never as current.
- [ ] Planted negative: Currency fixtures distinguish behind/current/unknown/absent and below-hold; a comparator mutant goes RED; the doctor makes no change to any installed tool.
- [ ] Independent/real machine: A non-implementer runs the currency scope live in Josh's real HOME and cites the report against actual installed versions and the uds policy file.
- [ ] Scope: Install-source changes, cadence updater, receipts, rollback, real update round and PI1 rerun moved to uds Stage 1 per comment #593; not required here.
- [ ] No-Claim: The currency report does not update anything or prove post-update compatibility.
issues.notes: State 2026-10-04: narrowed by comment #593 to a READ-ONLY installed-vs-latest report with hold warnings. uds Stage 1 owns update-source selection, the cadence updater, receipts and rollback (external: uds upgrade_policy.toml). JS1 reads that policy file; no update actions here.
